rationale: The COALESCE fallback is a coverage patch dressed as a measurement hierarchy — the cash-flow accrual ratio and the cash share of current assets are not the same construct and their rank distributions are not comparable, so the resulting signal changes economic meaning across subsamples (and across time as cash-flow-statement availability grew), producing exactly the unstable portfolio composition the objective warns against; both legs are also already in the archive.

A coherent, non-redundant pairing of the archive's strongest efficiency leg with a sales-deflated Sloan accrual, though the stated motivation is partly wrong (IND_RANK is monotone, so it does not "repair" outlier explosion, only the sign-flip pathology when act−che crosses zero) and the accrual leg is close to a textbook published anomaly.

Cumulating accruals over three years is a defensible horizon test that isolates the non-reversing component, but it edges toward rediscovering the net-operating-assets/long-run-accrual anomaly (cumulative accruals are mechanically the accrual stock), so the incremental content over the one-year version in the archive may be modest.

This is a cosmetic substitution of the bonus variable into an already twice-tested additive gated structure, and the reasoning is internally inconsistent — INDICATOR(oiadp,0) gates on profitability, not on cash-flow-statement availability, so the claimed coverage cushion does not follow (missing oancf will propagate to the sum, not fall back to the profit leg).

Both legs have independently strong records and the payables treatment genuinely differentiates them, but che/act and −(act−che−(lct−dlc))/at are mechanically negatively linked through che, so this risks being an averaging of two overlapping proxies rather than a test of complementarity.

A legitimate discriminating test of whether the accrual-stock leg adds information once profitability is already cash-based, well posed against the archive, though it is a straight leg-swap of two previously tested components and inherits the ~8% coverage of the oancf-based margin.
